newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's citrus exports to drop to 550,000T 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's citrus exports to drop to 550,000T 96/97.

text.p: Morocco's citrus exports are expected to drop by nearly 100,000 tonnes to 550,000 tonnes in 1996/97 due to sluggish consumption on the European market, Morocco's citrus association said on Monday.
"We expect total citrus exports to reach 550,000 tonnes by end of this season against 625,000 tonnes in 1995/96 period," a spokesman for the association said.
Morocco exported 461,000 tonnes of citrus this year, slightly up from 510,000 tonnes in the same period last year. But exports have stagnated in recent weeks, he added.
According to a Casablanca-based market analyst, Moroccan exporters failed to increase their European market share this year "because of sluggish consumption."

The European market has remained Morocco's main destination for citrus exports since 1975, he said but this year for the first time, Morocco exported 2,400 tonnes of citrus to the Gulf region, including the United Arab Emirates.
The country's main fruit and citrus farming areas are located in Souss and northern Gharb provinces.
